findings.element: .b-stamp — the footer's "Updated 15 July 2026", on every owner and guest surface (phone y1744, desk y1561, print y969, owner y1998)
findings.problem: The only string in the product that dates the plan is written by hand in one branch instead of by the one function every change already passes through, so it is false after five of the six things an owner can do. Driven at 1440x960 on BOTH grounds, owner-flight, harvesting .b-stamp before and after each mutation: move +7 -> "Updated 15 July 2026"; typed date -> "15 July"; rename -> "15 July"; hide -> "15 July"; delete -> "15 July"; add -> "Updated 16 July 2026". Identical on paper and ink. I deleted eight of the nine forward moments one after another and the footer still read "Updated 15 July 2026". render-b.js:1256-1261 sets F.updatedLabel inside the add branch only, under a comment that states the rule the other five break: "The stamp moves, because the plan just changed." This is not the round-7 freshness-stamp-is-decoration item, which was killed on co-visibility with "Live since 15 July" (~1800px apart, different registers); that objection is untouched here, because the reader who is misled is the guest, on a surface where "Live since" does not exist and the stamp is the only freshness claim there is. A couple opening the plan the evening the planner moved their dress fitting are told it was last updated eleven days ago. The gate already treats a stale timestamp as a defect in two places (interaction-check.mjs:2297 "the morning carries no stale timestamp", 2322 "a project with nothing in it claims no update"); the mutation path is the hole between them.
findings.fix: Hoist the two lines from the add branch at render-b.js:1260-1261 — F.updatedLabel = F.fmt.medium(F.today) + " " + F.fmt.year(F.today); paintPublication(root); — into remember(root, entry) at render-b.js:637, immediately before paintUndo(root). All six mutations (render-b.js:914, 942, 974, 1074, 1231, 1269) already route through it, so one writer then stamps every reversible change and no call site can forget. Delete the now-duplicate pair from the add branch. Leave the label alone on undo: the record was touched today whether or not the change survived.

findings.element: .b-pressTitle on the publish screen, 48px/600 — the draft branch, after pressing Copy the link
findings.problem: Drive owner-draft -> Publish -> Copy the link at 1440x960, both grounds. Before the press the heading reads "Send it to Mara & Finn." After it, takeTheLink() (render-b.js:1811-1821) rewrites it to "Mara & Finn have had this since 16 July." — 16 July being today. Present perfect with "since" states elapsed possession; here the elapsed time is zero and the possession has not happened. The screen then carries three statements of one fact at once and the loudest is the false one: the 48px headline says they have had it since today, the strap beside it still reads SENDING COMES NEXT, and the live region under it says "Link copied. Mara & Finn can open this now." Copying a link to your own clipboard is not handing it to anyone, and the page's own next line says so. The wording is right on the other branch — owner-flight -> Get the link gives "Mara & Finn have had this since 15 July." against a publishedAt genuinely in the past — so the sentence fits a plan somebody is already holding and not one that became live half a second ago. Round 10's fix was "taking the link publishes and rewrites the heading in place", and interaction-check.mjs:3059-3067 asserts only that the heading CHANGES (headBefore !== headAfter); neither the lock nor the gate requires this wording, so correcting it leaves both green.
findings.fix: Derive the heading from elapsed days through one accessor rather than from the published flag. In states.publish (render-b.js:1843-1846) and in takeTheLink (render-b.js:1817-1820) compute var since = F.publication.publishedAt ? F.days(F.publication.publishedAt, F.today) : -1; then write: since >= 1 ? F.project.name + " have had this since " + F.fmt.medium(F.publication.publishedAt) + "." : since === 0 ? F.project.name + " can open this as soon as you send it." : "Send it to " + F.project.name + ".". The just-published headline then agrees with the strap and with the live region instead of contradicting both, and the possessive sentence is kept for the case that earns it.

findings.element: .b-ceiling (#b-edit-when-hint), the editor's When field on owner-editing
findings.problem: Clear the date field and press Enter: the refusal reads "That is not a date. Try 3 October 2026." Nothing typed is not an unreadable date, and the product already knows this. The first field it ever offers splits the same three cases into three sentences — "Type the day first. For example, 3 October 2026." / "That is not a date. Try 3 October 2026." / "That day has gone. Pick one still ahead." — under a comment naming the defect verbatim ("One refusal for an empty field, an unreadable date and a day that has already gone told a typist to type"), and interaction-check.mjs:1514-1516 gates all three. commitDate (render-b.js:1044-1057) has only two branches, so the class the build fixed once is still standing in the editor an owner uses every week. Driven at 1440x960 on both grounds; identical.
findings.fix: In commitDate (render-b.js:1048-1052) test the raw value before the parse: var typed = (input.value || "").trim(); if (!typed) return refuse("Type the day first. For example, 3 October 2026."); placed above the existing if (!iso) return refuse("That is not a date. Try 3 October 2026."); — same three sentences, same order, same grammar as the first field.

biggestWin: The vocabulary of refusal and limit. Nothing here greys out, absorbs a press or hides behind a generic error: the stepper at the end of its range says "This is as far as it goes. Nothing can sit after the day itself." and at the other end "This is as near as it goes. Tomorrow is the soonest." — two sentences in one grammar that name the boundary and the reason, with the control's box identical before and after. The first field the product ever offers splits three failures into three true sentences. The stalled load says three different things in three voices without repeating a clause: "This is taking longer than it should." on the face, "Trying again." while it works, then "Still not arriving. The plan has not been deleted, and the link still works." — and the note it replaces is removed rather than printed twice. The countdown answers with a state rather than a string so a guest is never shown a negative, and the plural lives in one function so "1 days" cannot happen. The palette is spent, not obeyed: indigo lands on exactly two objects on the owner screen, carries the forward measure at a per-ground alpha that is re-earned rather than reused, and appears nowhere on publish, unfurl, ended or the empty project. Copy is byte-identical across paper and ink at all fourteen states, with no clip, no ellipsis and no horizontal scroll at 390, 768, 1152, 1279, 1280 or 1440.
